newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to cut charges at Jordanian border.
newsitem.headline: Israel to cut charges at Jordanian border.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Merdior said on Sunday he had ordered reductions in fees charged at the country's border with Jordan.

The Treasury said charges on bulk goods would be reduced 50 percent to 2.4 shekels per metric ton. The fees for business people and others making frequent border crossings will be reduced to $3.50 from $5 and fees for workers crossing on a regular basis to about $2 from $5.
The Treasury said Meridor decided to take the measures after a one-day visit to Jordan two weeks ago to discuss joint economic ussues.

They come on the back of other measures taken by the two countries in recent weeks, among them to allow entry of trucks from one country to the other and more frequent air connections. Israel has also widened the list of Jordanian goods entitled to reduced duties and has agreed to help foster direct trade between Jordan and the Palestinian areas.

"Despite this, economic relations with Jordan suffer in certain cases from bureaucratic redtape between the two countries," the Treasury said. "The finance ministry intends to find solutions in coordination with the Jordanian government."
